'''Sylvanus A. Tyler Sr.''' (August 21, 1914 – July 23, 1986) was an American mathematician and biostatistician.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Tyler |first1=Sylvanus A. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=X3hqNU5T_t0C&q=Sylvanus+A.+Tyler |title=On the Determination of Retention Behavior and Expected Total Metabolic Excretion of Radioisotopes from Daily Excretion Data |last2=Gurian |first2=Joan |date=1951 |publisher=Argonne National Laboratory |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Olinick |first=Michael |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fdC4EAAAQBAJ&dq=Sylvanus+A.+Tyler&pg=PA173 |title=Mathematical Modeling in the Social and Life Sciences |date=2014-05-05 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-1-118-64269-6 |language=en}}</ref> Tyler worked on the [[Manhattan Project]] at the [[Argonne National Laboratory]], where he was one of the few African American mathematicians assigned to the project.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=1986-07-26 |title=Obituary - Sylvanus A. Tyler, Sr. |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1986/07/26/sylvanus-a-tyler-sr/ |access-date=2024-02-28 |website=Chicago Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Tyler was born in Chicago in 1914 and attended city public schools. He earned an undergraduate degree from [[Fisk University]] and a master's degree from the [[University of Chicago]]. During [[World War II]], Tyler served in the [[United States Army Signal Corps]] and was stationed in Italy.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=1986-07-29 |title=SYLVANUS TYLER, 71, ARGONNE BIOSTATISTICIAN |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1986/07/29/sylvanus-tyler-71-argonne-biostatistician/ |access-date=2024-02-28 |website=Chicago Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>

Tyler becan working at the Argonne National Laboratory in 1946 and worked at the lab for 34 years, retiring in 1980. Tyler also served as faculty at [[Tougaloo College]] and [[Alabama A&M University]]. Tyler was published in over 75 journal articles during his career.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Michael Fry |first1=R. J. |last2=Staffeldt |first2=Everett |last3=Tyler |first3=Sylvanus A. |date=1978-01-01 |title=Some problems arising in analysis of large-scale animal irradiation experiments |url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0160-4120%2878%2990015-6 |journal=Environment International |volume=1 |issue=6 |pages=361–366 |doi=10.1016/0160-4120(78)90015-6 |bibcode=1978EnInt...1..361M |issn=0160-4120|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=U-lcwvPs0FgC&dq=Sylvanus+A.+Tyler&pg=PA2695 |title=Nuclear Science Abstracts |date=1967 |publisher=Oak Ridge Directed Operations, Technical Information Division |language=en}}</ref>

After his retirement, Tyler continued to support the Argonne lab and the [[United States Department of the Interior]] as a statistical consultant.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Tyler, Sylvanus A. |url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=7103350198 |access-date=2024-02-28 |website=www.scopus.com}}</ref>

== Death ==
Tyler died in July 1986 at the age of 71. His obituary was published in the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]''.<ref name=":0" />

==Recognition==
In 1949, Tyler was featured in an ''[[Ebony (magazine)|Ebony]]'' magazine article titled "Atom Scientists: Ten Negro Scientists at Argonne Lab Help in Race to Harness Atomic Materials."
